agent_notes: Diff only removes a Math.min(100, ...) clamp on a numeric download-percentage calculation in view-file.service.ts (src/angular/src/app/services/files/view-file.service.ts:307-309). Verified downstream usage: the value is bound via Angular interpolation `{{ file.percentDownloaded | number:'1.0-1' }}%` (auto-escaped, numeric only) and the progress-bar width binding in transfer-row.component.html:35 already has its own independent clamp (`file.percentDownloaded > 100 ? 100 : ...`). No injection, XSS, auth, secrets, or other security-relevant sink is reachable from this value. This is a UI correctness/display regression (percentages over 100% may now render as text, e.g. '199%'), not a security vulnerability, so no findings are reported.

This diff reverts commit 879266c ('fix(ui): clamp transfer progress at 100% for extracted files'). Unless an intent doc or commit message explains why, it looks like a regression rather than a design change. No intent context was provided.

Two test vectors in src/angular/src/app/tests/unittests/services/files/view-file.service.spec.ts at lines 246-247 ([20,10,100] and [100,50,100]) still expect the clamped value, so this change will fail the existing spec. That belongs to test-sufficiency/bugs, but it confirms that the clamp was a documented, intended contract.

Grep shows percentDownloaded is read only in transfer-row.component.html and in test fixtures. dashboard-stats.service.ts, view-file-filter.service.ts and view-file-sort.service.ts do not read it, so the blast radius is limited to the transfer row UI.

The inline clamp on template line 35 (`> 100 ? 100 : < 0 ? 0 : ...`) is defensive duplication that was harmless while the service clamped. With the service clamp removed it becomes the only guard, and it covers only the bar width.
No import cycles, new dependencies, cross-module reach-ins, or rule-of-three duplication were introduced.

findings.fix_hint: restore Math.min(100, ...) in the service so ViewFile keeps its 0-100 contract; if raw ratios are needed, add a separate field instead of overloading percentDownloaded
findings.problem: ViewFileService is where raw ModelFile values become display-ready ViewFile state, and commit 879266c deliberately made it keep percentDownloaded within 0-100. Its one consumer, src/angular/src/app/pages/files/transfer-row.component.html, does not handle values above 100. Line 35 clamps only the bar width. Line 28 prints the raw value, so an extracted file can show '199%'. Lines 33 and 53 test `=== 100`, so an over-100 extracted file loses the success bar style and the 'Done' ETA label. The fix for one problem now sits half in the service and half in the template.
findings.title: Removing the clamp breaks the ViewFile percentDownloaded 0-100 contract and pushes normalization onto consumers that only partly handle it
findings.why_it_matters: Every consumer of ViewFile now has to clamp the value itself. The current template already misses the label and the two `=== 100` checks, so finished extracted files show over 100% and never reach the 'Done' state.

agent_notes: Change: the service's percentDownloaded computation no longer clamps at 100. This loosens an output-bounding control that commit 879266c deliberately added for extracted files (unpacked size > archive size).

Consumers I read with a grep across src/angular/src/app: the only runtime consumer of percentDownloaded is pages/files/transfer-row.component.html (lines 24, 28, 33, 35, 53). dashboard-stats, view-file-filter and view-file-sort import ViewFileService but do not read percentDownloaded.

The template partly compensates: bar width is clamped inline at line 35. It does not compensate in three places: the label (line 28 shows e.g. '200%'), the success class (line 33, === 100), and the ETA 'Done' state (line 53, === 100). All three break for any extracted file where local > remote.
No public API, type or schema change. ViewFile.percentDownloaded is still number | null. No backend, DB or performance impact; the change is pure arithmetic per file per model update.
Blast radius: one UI row component, but every user of the transfer table who extracts archives sees it. Tests: view-file.service.spec.ts lines 245-246 will fail.
Verdict: Blocking issue. This reverts a shipped UI fix and breaks an existing unit test. Restore Math.min(100, ...) unless the reversal is intentional and the template and tests are updated to match.
